title: Keep Your Own Books
subtitle: A bookkeeping routine for freelancers and sole traders, from the first invoice to a month you can close in an hour
author: The Velvet Foundry Editorial Team
description:
You started working for yourself, somebody said "keep your books", and nobody explained what that meant. You now have a business bank account, a folder of receipts, a spreadsheet you abandoned, and a quiet worry that you are doing it wrong.

This book teaches one system: the same double-entry method every accountant uses, which has five moving parts and can be learned in an afternoon by anyone who can add. Not software. The system underneath the software, so you stop being at its mercy.

WHAT YOU WILL BE ABLE TO DO: record any transaction your business can produce; prove your records against your bank statement; close a month in about an hour; and read your own profit and loss and balance sheet without anyone translating them for you.

WHAT IS INSIDE: 21 chapters across the five kinds of account, double entry without the jargon, a working chart of accounts you can copy, recording money in and out, cash basis against accrual, the bank reconciliation, drawings and owner's money, untangling mixed personal spending, a one-hour month-end routine, reading both statements, a full month worked end to end from opening balance to closing statements, what records to keep, what your accountant actually wants, and when to stop doing this yourself. Every chapter ends with the ways it goes wrong and a checklist.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT: it contains no tax rates, thresholds, deadlines or filing rules. That is deliberate. Those are specific to your country and they change, so a book stating them would be wrong for most readers on the day it shipped, and wrong in a way that looked authoritative. This book teaches the part that is the same everywhere and does not expire: how to record what happened. It names the three questions only a local professional can answer, and tells you to go and ask them.

WHO IT IS FOR: sole traders, freelancers, independent contractors and single-owner businesses doing their own books, with no accounting background assumed.

WHO SHOULD NOT BUY IT: if you employ people and need payroll, if you run an incorporated company with filing obligations, or if you want to be told your tax rates and deadlines, this is the wrong book and it says so in chapter 2.

FORMAT: reflowable EPUB, about 15,000 words, readable on a phone. No worksheets to print or write into.

General educational material about bookkeeping method. Not accounting, tax, legal or financial advice.
categories: Business & Money > Small Business & Entrepreneurship > Accounting
note: Scope is deliberately mechanics only: how to record, prove and summarise transactions. It contains no tax rates, thresholds, deadlines, filing instructions or jurisdiction-specific rules, by design, because The Velvet Foundry has no licensed tax professional on staff and those rules differ by country and change. Every point where a jurisdiction rule is needed is flagged in the text and routed to the reader's own tax authority or a local professional, and the three such questions are collected in the closing chapter. Payroll, sales tax and VAT mechanics, and incorporated-company accounts are all explicitly out of scope and named as such in chapter 2. No source is cited with a page reference or a figure: organisations are named instead, because a stale citation is worse than none.
